title: Pure-tensor clopen restriction and flat/K-flat detection
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a finite set, and $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes covering $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Work on their small pro-etale sites in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, $R_i=R|_{X_i}$, and let $r_i$, $G$ and $e_i$ be the restriction, sectionwise product gluing, and zero insertion functors of [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

Use the sheafified sectionwise tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], unbounded cochain complexes and cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], flat module sheaves (tensoring is exact) [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and K-flat complexes (tensoring every acyclic complex gives an acyclic complex) [def-pc-kflat-complex]. There are natural isomorphisms
$$a_{i,F,H}:r_i(F\otimes_RH)\xrightarrow{\sim}r_iF\otimes_{R_i}r_iH,\qquad r_iR\cong R_i,$$
with $a_{i,F,H}(f\otimes h)=r_if\otimes r_ih$ on local sheafified pure tensors. These comparisons respect the ordinary associativity, symmetry, and both unit constraints. Restriction is left adjoint to $e_i$ and preserves every small coproduct in the fixed module universe.

For every pair $P,Q$ of unbounded $R$-complexes there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$b_{i,P,Q}:r_i\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(r_iP\otimes_{R_i}r_iQ),$$
whose map on the $(p,q)$ direct-sum summand is $a_{i,P^p,Q^q}$. It preserves the summand inclusion and has differential formula
$$x\otimes y\longmapsto r_i(dx)\otimes r_iy+(-1)^p r_ix\otimes r_i(dy).$$
The isomorphism is natural on all chain maps and compatible with the signed symmetries of the total tensor complexes, which send $x\otimes y$ with $x\in P^p$, $y\in Q^q$ to $(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ (and likewise for $r_iP,r_iQ$).

For every $R$-module sheaf $F$, flatness of $F$ is equivalent to flatness of every $r_iF$. For every unbounded $R$-complex $P$, K-flatness of $P$ is equivalent to K-flatness of every $r_iP$, without assuming boundedness or flat terms. All assertions include empty components, the empty covering partition, and zero ring sheaves.
